THIS MFA FILED U/S 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED:04.05.2015 PASSED IN MVC NO.44/2013 ON THE FILE OF THE ADDITIONAL SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND MACT XIII, MADHUGIRI, AWARD OF AMOUNT OF RS.5,27,228/- ALONG WITH INTEREST AT 6% P.A. FROM THE DATE OF THE PETITION IS DEPOSITED.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed under Section-173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'MV Act' for brevity) by the appellant-insurance company, calling in question the judgment and award dated 04.05.2015, passed in M.V.C.No.44/2013, on the file of the Additional Senior Civil Judge And MACT XIII, Madhugiri (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal' for brevity) stating that the claimant himself had fallen from the bike and had sustained injuries.
Brief facts:
2. On 09.05.2012, at about 9.30 p.m., when the claimant was proceeding in the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-06-EE-0072 as a pillion rider and proceeding to Hosakere.

At that time, when the said vehicle came near Muthurayanaswamy Temple, Lakshmidevipura on Rantavalalu-Hosakere road, Madhugiri at that point of time, the driver of the motor cycle is said to have driven the same in high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed a Dog and caused accident.
On account of the road traffic accident, the claimant is said to have fallen from the motor cycle and sustained head injury and injury to other parts of the body.

3. Hence, a claim petition was filed by the claimant under Section-166 of the M.V.
Act, claiming compensation for the injuries suffered in the accident.

The Tribunal on appreciating the materials on record, allowed the claim petition in part, and awarded M/S. Tata Aig General Insurance Company ... vs Rajanna D on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193749173/
2 a compensation of Rs.5,27,228/-, along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realisation.

sentences.text: The Tribunal held respondent Nos.1 and 2 therein, liable to pay the compensation.

4. Heard arguments of the learned counsel for the parties and perused the materials on record.
5.

The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the claimant himself was driving the motor cycle and due to rash and negligent driving, he had fallen on the ground and the same is reflected in the medical records.
Hence, the claim petition is not maintainable.
Further, submitted that there is a delay of 35 days in lodging the complaint.
Hence, in order to make false claim against the insurance company, a story is created that one Nanjappa, was driving the motor cycle and the claimant was the pillion.

Therefore,
at various point of time when the claimant was admitted in the hospital he has stated to the hospital authorities that he had fallen from the bike himself and therefore the claim petition is not maintainable.
Therefore, prays to allow the appeal by setting-aside the impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal.

6. On the other hand, the learned counsel for the respondent - claimant, submitted that the one Nanjappa was driving the motor cycle and he caused the accident and in this regard a complaint was lodged.
Thereafter, resultantly a charge-sheet was also filed against the rider of the motorcycle Nanjappa.
Therefore, submitted that the Police record prove that the claimant was pillion rider.
Hence, the Tribunal is correct in allowing the claim petition.
Further, submitted that mere delay in lodging the complaint cannot be a ground to reject the claim petition, since the claimant was admitted in NIMHANS Hospital, Bengaluru for a period of 21 days.
Therefore, he could not lodge the complaint on time.
Therefore, there is a delay.
Hence, prays to dismiss the appeal of the insurance company.

7. In the present case, as per the complaint averments one Nanjappa was driving the motor cycle and the claimant was the pillion rider and the driver caused the accident by driving the same in high speed and in a rash and negligent manner.

Upon police investigation, a charge-sheet was filed against the driver of the offending motor cycle one Nanjappa and there was a delay of 35 days in lodging the complaint.
8.
Undisputedly, the accident was caused on 09.05.2012, and the complaint was lodged on 14.06.2012.

Quite naturally, PW-1, claimant gave evidence before the Tribunal that Nanjappa was driving the motor cycle and that he was a pillion rider, but there is no evidence on record whether Nanjappa sustained injuries or not.
PW-2 is said to be an eye-witness and he has deposed that he witnessed the accident, but he has not lodged the complaint before the Police.
He simply appears as eye- witness to the accident.
Therefore, he has not lodged any complaint.
Hence, it may be presumed that PW-2 may be a planted witness for the purpose of the case.

sentences.text: Upon perusing the medical records Exhibit-R7, hospital case records, the history is mentioned as the claimant has fallen from the bike and even it is mentioned in the case records / inpatient records that the claimant while driving the motor bike had fallen from the bike and sustained injuries.
The entries made in these records plays a significant role in assessing what would have happened.
These evidences of hospital records are prepared at very much initial point of time i.e., soon after the accident, when the claimant was admitted to the hospital.

Therefore, the hospital authorities /
doctors have noted down the history of alleged accident.
It carries more weightage than other documents.
Charge-sheet may be filed against Nanjappa, based on the complaint and FIR, but complaint is lodged after 35 days from the date of accident.
Therefore, there may be chances of manipulation in lodging the complaint just to make claim against the insurance company.
Therefore, considering the evidence as discussed above on all its preponderance of probabilities, it is proved that the claimant while driving the motor cycle had sustained injuries.
The complaint lodged is an after-thought just to make the claim against the insurance company.
10. The documentary evidence which are medical evidence speaks themselves of really what has happened.
In this regard, the particulars noted down by the Hospital authorities in the natural course of time can be believed as they are having more weightage than other documents.

Especially,
in cases like present nature, where there is a delay of 35 days in filing the complaint and the contents of the complaint are perverse and contrary to the medical records.
Therefore, the finding of the Tribunal that the insurance company is liable to pay compensation is liable to be set-aside.
As it is stated in the medical records, that the claimant himself has fallen and sustained injuries, the question of claiming compensation from insurance company does not arise.
Hence, the claim petition is liable to be dismissed.
For the aforesaid reasons, the appeal is liable to be allowed by setting aside the judgment and award of the Tribunal.

11. Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i. The appeal is Allowed.
ii. The impugned judgment and award dated 04.05.2015, passed in M.V.C.No.44/2013, on - 10 - the file of the Additional Senior Civil Judge And MACT XIII, Madhugiri is Set-Aside.
iii. The amount in deposit shall be refunded to the by the Appellant - Insurance company.
iv. Registry is directed to return the Trial Court Records to the Tribunal, along with certified copy of the order passed by this Court forthwith without any delay.
v. No order as to costs.
